subject: Follow-up: ClearBank concurrency & streaming SLOs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearbank.com>
Cc: ClearBank SRE <sre@clearbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Follow-up: ClearBank concurrency & streaming SLOs

Hi Sara / ClearBank team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment overall. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can finalize the quota proposal:

- Traffic shape: you mentioned a steady baseline of ~600 concurrent requests during trading hours with two 10–15 minute spikes up to ~2,200 concurrent streaming sessions. Confirmed?
- Latency SLO: 95th %ile generation latency target is 400ms for non-streaming calls and 150ms tail for streaming tokens.
- Streaming: you plan to use chunked streaming (SSE/HTTP2) for market commentary; longest sessions ~18 minutes, average ~3 minutes.
- Multiplexing/keepalives: you prefer long-lived connections and client-side multiplexing (2–4 logical streams per TCP connection) to reduce connection churn.

Open questions for our infra team:
1) Do you expect long idle periods between tokens within a session (e.g., >20s pauses)?
2) Any hard QPS limits per customer region (EU-only traffic) or internal throttles we should reflect in the proposal?
3) Are there any regulatory constraints on burst buffering or caching of prompts on our side?

Next steps: I'll circulate a revised quota proposal and an MAP (mutual action plan) with dates. If the numbers above are off, tell me the corrected baseline/spike figures and we'll update.

Attaching a first-pass quota worksheet and a draft MAP for your review.

Cheers,

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0192

Attachments: conn_quota_proposal_v2.pdf (summary), clearbank_mutual_action_plan.xlsx
From: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearBank SRE <sre@clearbank.com>
Date: Thu, 02 May 2028 10:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ClearBank concurrency & streaming SLOs

Thanks Soojin — that summary is accurate with one clarification: the 2,200 spike is per region (we will run EU primary, but we may failover to a UK secondary region occasionally). A few notes from SRE:

- Idle pauses: yes, some sessions have multi-second pauses while clients aggregate events. Not typically >25s but there are edge cases up to ~40s.
- Multiplexing: we will multiplex on our side but only 1–2 logical streams per connection for the first phase.
- Regulatory: no customer data should be persisted outside EU. Short-term prompt-level caching for repeated queries is OK if restricted to EU nodes.

Can Redwood support a token-burst bucket that allows short spikes up to 3x baseline for up to 30s? If not, what is the recommended pattern to avoid dropped streams?

Sara
Sara Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearBank
sara.chen@clearbank.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 08:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Fwd: ClearBank concurrency details — need recommendation on temporary burst handling

Karthik / Marcus — forwarding ClearBank's clarifications. Key asks: support EU-only retention, token-burst bucket up to 3x baseline for ~30s, tolerate up to 40s idle in some sessions, and initial multiplexing 1–2 streams/connection.

Questions for runtime:
- Can we provision a per-customer burst bucket that won't impact other tenants? If yes, how to express that in a quota?
- Idle timeouts & connection pooling: what's the safe keepalive window to avoid eviction while preserving slot efficiency?
- Streaming tail-latency: will prioritizing streaming sessions affect non-streaming 95p in the same pool?

Please reply with a concise ops recommendation and numbers we can send back to ClearBank. I plan to send them a formal quota sheet by Monday.

— Soojin
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 May 2028 11:42:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: ClearBank concurrency details — need recommendation on temporary burst handling

Soojin — quick recommendation from infra/serving:

1) Quotas (initial):
   - Reserved concurrency tokens: baseline 600 concurrent sessions (EU pool).
   - Burst capacity: short-term burst bucket of +1,200 tokens (3x baseline) that drains over a 30s window. Implement as a token-bucket tied to the customer's project id; bucket refills at baseline rate.
   - Max sustained cap: 2,400 concurrent sessions to prevent noisy-neighbor risk.

2) Connection pooling & multiplexing:
   - Recommend keepalive window 45s for EU customers with long-session flag. That allows the 40s edge-case without eviction and keeps pool slot churn low.
   - Support 1–2 logical streams per TCP by default; allow configurable multiplexing up to 4 streams in later phases.

3) Streaming & latency impact:
   - Prioritize active streaming pipelines via soft-priority lanes; streaming tokens are routed to low-latency lanes with reserved micro-batches. This will add modest tail pressure on non-streaming workloads only under sustained >80% utilization.
   - For ClearBank's projected shape, keep lanes dedicated in EU pool; expected 95p non-streaming latency with these configs: ~380–420ms depending on model and sequence length distribution.

4) Compliance & caching:
   - We can scope caching and ephemeral KV to EU-only nodes and include that in the MAP. No prompt persistence outside EU.

Operational notes: add an automatic fallback policy to a slightly lower-capacity model variant if sustained usage hits 95% of the max sustained cap — this avoids hard drops.

I attached a compact quota table (conn_quota_proposal_v2.pdf) with computed cost delta for Reserved vs. Burst options. Marcus — flag anything I missed.

— Karthik
Head of Serving Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Sara Chen <sara.chen@clearbank.com>, ClearBank SRE <sre@clearbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 15:28:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: ClearBank concurrency & streaming SLOs — proposal attached

Hi Sara — sharing the recommended configuration from infra and a short MAP with milestones (attached). Highlights:

- Baseline reserved concurrency: 600 sessions (EU pool)
- Burst bucket: +1,200 tokens (30s drain) — intended for market-open spikes
- Max sustained cap: 2,400 sessions; automatic fallback to next-best model at 95% threshold
- Keepalive: 45s for flagged long sessions; multiplexing 1–2 streams initially
- EU-only caching for repeated prompts; no cross-region persistence

Ask: can your SRE confirm that 45s keepalive fits your networking setup? Also confirm final go-live target date (we tentatively set 2028-05-20 in the MAP).

Next steps: once you confirm, we’ll provision the reserved baseline and enable the burst bucket for a 30-day evaluation. We’ll run a short soak test during market open next week (dates in MAP).

Thanks — attaching conn_quota_proposal_v2.pdf and clearbank_mutual_action_plan.xlsx again.

Best,

— Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
